newsitem.title: GERMANY: Kohl, Yeltsin confident of Russia-NATO deal.
newsitem.headline: Kohl, Yeltsin confident of Russia-NATO deal.

text.p: President Boris Yeltsin and German Chancellor Helmut Kohl expressed optimism on Thursday Russia and NATO could agree on the Atlantic Alliance's eastward expansion before a planned summit in Paris on May 27.

Yeltsin, looking tired and pale after a day of talks with his friend and ally in the German spa town of Baden-Baden, said: "We want to announce...that on the 27th of May in Paris the agreement will be signed by the leaders of the NATO countries and of Russia."

"So we need to hurry," Yeltsin added. It marked something of a change in tone from remarks by his spokesman on the eve of the talks, who said Yeltsin would not sign any deal that failed to give Russia strict security guarantees.
Russia's demands that NATO agree to limit the stationing of foreign troops in east European countries that join the alliance have held up preparations for the planned May 27 summit.
NATO Secretary-General Javier Solana said on Wednesday the talks might not be completed in time for the Paris meeting.
Kohl said the document was mostly finished but some parts needed more work urgently. He and Yeltsin declined to give any details.
Kohl, who called Yeltsin "dear Boris", said Germany would help find a solution but would not play the role of an interpreter.
"I am confident that, with good will on both sides, we can come to an agreement before the NATO-Russia summit on May 27," he said.
He noted however that, while four chapters of the treaty were "90 percent" complete, a fifth posed significant problems.
Yeltsin repeated Russia's insistence on a say in NATO decision-making through consensus and that nuclear and conventional weapons not be deployed closer to Russia's borders.
